test_title: PYST 30: SSC GD Constable 2025 - General Knowledge (Held On: 18 Feb, 2025 - Shift 3)
subject: gk
question:
Match the following items.

 
 

 Name of the Scheme
 Year
 
 

 i. Jawahar Rozgar Yojana
 1. 1988
 
 

 ii. The Employee Assurance Scheme
 2. 1989
 
 

 iii. The Million Wells Scheme
 3. 1995
 
 

 iv. National Social Assistance Programme
 4. 1993
solution:
The correct answer is __**i-2, ii-4, iii-1, iv-3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (1989):**

 
 
• Launched in **1989** by merging earlier rural employment programs like NREP (National Rural Employment Programme) and RLEGP (Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme).
 
• Objective: To provide employment to the unemployed in rural areas and create durable community assets.
 
• Implemented as a centrally sponsored scheme with a 80:20 cost-sharing ratio between the Centre and the states.
 
 
 
• **The Employee Assurance Scheme (1993):**
 
 
• Launched in **1993** as part of the social security initiatives for employees.
 
• Objective: To provide financial assurance to employees and their families in case of untimely death or disability.
 
• This scheme primarily benefited employees working in the organized sector.
 
 
 
• **The Million Wells Scheme (1988):**
 
 
• Launched in **1988** as a sub-scheme of the National Rural Employment Programme (NREP).
 
• Objective: To provide irrigation facilities and ensure water availability to small and marginal farmers, particularly those living below the poverty line.
 
• It emphasized developing sustainable agricultural practices.
 
 
 
• **National Social Assistance Programme (1995):**
 
 
• Launched in **1995** as part of a broader social welfare initiative by the Government of India.
 
• Objective: To provide financial support to the elderly, widows, and persons with disabilities belonging to below-poverty-line families.
 
• The scheme includes components like the National Old Age Pension Scheme (NOAPS) and the National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jawahar Rozgar Yojana:**

 
 
• The scheme was later revamped into other rural employment programs like the Sampoorna Gramin Rozgar Yojana (SGRY) and subsequently the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS).
 
• It primarily targeted rural poverty alleviation by providing wage employment opportunities to below-poverty-line families.
 
 
 
• **The Million Wells Scheme:**
 
 
• This scheme focused on small and marginal farmers, enabling them to improve their agricultural productivity through better irrigation facilities.
 
• It was particularly beneficial in areas with water scarcity and drought-prone regions.
 
 
 
• **National Social Assistance Programme:**
 
 
• It was one of the first centrally sponsored schemes aimed at providing a safety net to vulnerable sections of society.
 
• Components like widow pensions and family benefits have been crucial in reducing the financial burden on marginalized families.
 
 
 
• **Employee Assurance Scheme:**
 
 
• The scheme complemented other social security measures like the Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) and the Employees’ State Insurance (ESI).
 
• It emphasized creating a financial safety net for employees working in the formal sector.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Jawahar Rozgar Yojana** is considered a precursor to the modern MGNREGS, which guarantees 100 days of wage employment to rural households.
 
• **The Million Wells Scheme** is notable for its focus on sustainable agriculture and groundwater management.
 
• **National Social Assistance Programme** has evolved to include various direct benefit transfer mechanisms to ensure financial aid reaches beneficiaries directly.
 
• **Employee Assurance Scheme** paved the way for more comprehensive insurance schemes for employees in the organized sector.
